episodes.title: FBI Intel Cuts, Patriot Batteries in Poland & the Proton's Baryon Junction
episodes.subject: Hourly sourced brief: FBI counterintelligence shifts, JIATF 401 counter-drone energy picks, Poland deploying Patriots with $26B civil defense plan, Black Sea merchant vessel drone strikes, AI threats to independent science, baryon junctions in proton structure, and pulvinar stimulation of visual percepts.
paragraphs: Welcome back to ZeroFilter. It is zero-four-hundred hours UTC. In Washington, NPR reports the FBI's counterintelligence divisions are falling behind as leadership redirects agents toward immigration sweeps, leaving foreign espionage operations unmonitored. Meanwhile, the War Department announced its directed-energy selections for the JIATF 401 pilot, betting on high-powered microwaves and combat lasers to down drone swarms. Dismantling counterspy units while handing defense contractors billions for directed energy is not national defense. It is systemic institutional decay.

To the frontline. Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced Poland is deploying Patriot batteries near the Ukrainian border, backed by a twenty-six billion dollar civil defense package for hardened shelters, rescue bases, and emergency power. Across the Black Sea, Russian strikes hit international shipping. The Kyiv Independent reports drone attacks struck merchant vessels off Bulgaria and Ukraine, killing at least one civilian sailor on a Marshall Islands-flagged ship. Moscow claims defensive operations; the maritime receipts show blatant piracy.

Frontier compute. A new report in Nature warns that foundation models are quietly undermining scientific independence. As research labs rely on closed corporate AI pipelines for hypothesis generation and synthesis, academic agendas are subtly steered toward problems that private compute monopolies prioritize. Delegating scientific curiosity to black-box systems trained on proprietary benchmarks does not produce objective discovery; it builds an intellectual monoculture funded by public grants. Keep models open, or lose independent science.

Subatomic physics. Nature reports strong evidence from relativistic collisions that proton identity is anchored by gluonic baryon junctions, rather than valence quarks alone. The glue holding matter together has topological structure. Combine that with Wheeler's delayed-choice experiment, confirmed by Jacques and colleagues in Science: a photon exhibits wave or particle traits only after the detection setup is chosen. Physical reality has no definite path before measurement. The universe is participatory at its fundamental scale.

Consciousness desk. A new bioRxiv study shows electrical stimulation of the human pulvinar, a higher-order thalamic nucleus, directly generates conscious visual percepts in monitored patients. Subjective vision can be ignited deep in subcortical hubs without retinal input. Compare that to the declassified 1995 AIR review of CIA Project Stargate: while evaluators concluded remote viewing lacked operational consistency, laboratory trials documented statistically anomalous hit rates. The line between sensory routing and non-material awareness remains open.

Tonight's receipts. Counterintelligence gutting while counter-drone contracts surge. Poland fortifying its border as Black Sea shipping burns. Corporate compute steering scientific inquiry. Subatomic topology proving matter is relational, and thalamic stimulation generating synthetic perception. Both partisan tribes want you fearful and distracted. Reject the noise. Reality renders upon observation, so check the receipts in the dossier drawer, and stay lucid. I'm Rex Vance.

episodes.title: Pentagon Advisers' Conflicts, a Tanker Ablaze off Sochi & a Blueprint for Quantum Gravity
episodes.subject: Hourly sourced brief: ethics worries over Elon Musk's and Palmer Luckey's new Pentagon roles, the War Department's counter-drone laser and microwave picks, a shadow-fleet tanker reportedly ablaze near Sochi, Ukraine's drone-casualty tally, Yuri Shvets' broadcast #1216, error-correcting dynamics inside language models, a proposed test of gravity-induced entanglement, and how the brain recalibrates what feels simultaneous.
paragraphs: Welcome back to ZeroFilter. It is twenty-two hundred hours UTC. In Washington, NPR reports that Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey have taken new Pentagon roles, and ethics experts are worried: their companies, SpaceX and Anduril, could benefit from recommendations in a Pentagon study on future autonomous weapons. Same day, the War Department named the laser and microwave systems it selected after its JIATF 401 counter-drone pilot. My take: when the people advising on the shopping list also sell the merchandise, that is a conflict of interest.

To the Black Sea. The Kyiv Independent reports a shadow-fleet tanker reportedly ablaze near Sochi, and Russian Telegram channels suggest sea drones hit it. Robert Brovdi, call sign Madyar, who commands Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, says his units recorded 2,699 Russian troops killed or wounded from October 1 to 5, up from 1,931 in the same days of September. And in broadcast number 1216, Yuri Shvets lays out what he calls six priorities for victory: six lines of effort that must work at once, instead of slogans and promises of another counteroffensive.

Frontier compute. A new arXiv paper asks why language models stay coherent even when you shove their internal activations around, for example with steering. The authors' hypothesis is passive error correction: mechanisms in the forward pass that funnel activations back toward regions that produce sensible output, which the title calls privileged error-correcting basins. If that holds up, these models are sturdier than the parrot jokes suggest. That last part is my read, not their claim.

Quantum next. Nobody has yet caught gravity entangling two masses. Proposals argue that if gravity alone can do it, gravity itself must be quantum, and with the Planck scale out of reach, a tabletop interferometer is the realistic back door. A new arXiv paper works out the best interferometer geometry for that experiment. No result yet. This is a blueprint, not a discovery.

Consciousness desk. Your sense of at the same time is not fixed. A new bioRxiv study looks at rapid temporal recalibration: after signals from different senses arrive slightly out of sync, your judgment of what is simultaneous shifts toward that recent timing. The authors separate a genuine perceptual realignment from a decision-level carryover from your previous answers, and report that the two come apart across the senses. Part of what feels like perception is bookkeeping.

So, tonight's receipts. Two tech billionaires in Pentagon roles their companies could profit from. A tanker reportedly burning off Sochi. Drone casualty counts climbing, by Ukraine's own tally. A blueprint, not a breakthrough, for quantum gravity. And a brain that edits its own sense of now. Every one is linked in the source drawer. Read them yourself, and stay lucid. I'm Rex Vance.
